subject: Follow-up: data custody for prompt/response handling — summary & action items
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@healthiq.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: intro / demo — data custody follow-ups

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the SOW and security answers: 

Summary of your posture from the call:
- HealthIQ will send patient-facing free-text prompts to our inference API from the EU.
- You need assurance that raw PHI (names, MRNs, unredacted notes) is not retained beyond what is required for inference and debugging.
- You require audit logs for compliance for 12 months and EU residency for any persisted artifacts.

High-level answers / what Redwood can offer (need your confirmation on a couple of items below):
1) Hosted API (standard): prompts and generated outputs are not stored permanently by default. Ephemeral diagnostic logs are retained for 24 hours for debugging (can be disabled).
2) Dedicated / Private: retention windows are configurable; customers can request full retention controls and a contract-backed residency SLA (we can retain logs in an EU-only Dedicated pool).
3) KV/prefix cache behavior: session-only — cached tokens are evicted at session end and not written to long-term storage.
4) Audit trails: structured request/response metadata (no raw-output by default) can be exported to your SIEM; we can offer 12-month log retention in EU on Dedicated.

Questions for you so we can finalize answers in writing:
- Do you need raw prompt text or full outputs persisted anywhere (yes/no)? If yes, please indicate required retention and region.
- Is pseudonymization (hashing of identifiers) acceptable for any persisted logs?

Attachments: I attached a sample data map you mentioned in the call — please confirm the fields that will be sent.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to answer technical nuance below (cc).
- I’ll assemble a short security pack and proposed SOW language for residency/retention.
- Can we target sign-off on security posture by July 30 so procurement can start?

Thanks,

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@healthiq.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HealthIQ Legal <legal@healthiq.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 08:04:00 +0100
Subject: Re: intro / demo — data custody follow-ups

Soojin — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We cannot send unredacted PHI to any third-party that persists it beyond processing. Our procurement team will require explicit confirmation that Redwood does not retain raw prompts or outputs in Hosted mode.
- For Dedicated, if we opt for retention, it must be in an EU region and retention configurable to 12 months; any persisted data must be encrypted with customer-controlled keys (KMS).
- Audit logs: we need an immutable audit trail for requests (timestamps, request IDs, model used) for 12 months. We prefer logs exported to our Splunk instance but can accept hosted retention if contractually guaranteed.

Quick answers to your Qs:
- Do we need raw prompt text persisted? No — our preference is no long-term storage of raw prompts or outputs.
- Pseudonymization/hashing: acceptable for telemetry/aggregates, but not for raw clinical data used for primary diagnosis.

Legal wants an initial security pack (SOC2, encryption at rest/in transit, data residency options) and a one-page section to insert into the MSA about retention/residency.

I’ll loop in Legal for procurement; please push the security pack and proposed SOW language when ready.

Best,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Integrations | HealthIQ

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 08:27:00 +0100
Subject: Re: intro / demo — data custody follow-ups

Alex — wanted to add the technical detail so you have something concrete to pass to procurement/legal. Quoting key points from Soojin’s note and adding specifics: 

1) Hosted API (our standard public offering)
- Default behavior: we do not persist customer prompts or generated outputs to long-term object storage.
- Short-lived debugging logs: request metadata and truncated diagnostic payloads (not full outputs) are retained up to 24 hours in volatile stores to aid crash analysis; this can be disabled per-account.
- Telemetry: aggregated usage metrics (token counts, latency percentiles) are stored longer for billing and product analytics — these are pseudonymized and do not contain PHI fields.

2) Dedicated / Private deployment
- Retention config: Customers can request a specific retention window (e.g., 12 months) for request/response artifacts stored inside the Dedicated environment.
- Residency: we can guarantee EU-only storage and processing for the Dedicated cluster; we also support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption at rest.
- Audit logs: structured request metadata (request ID, timestamps, model/version, route) can be made immutable and exported to your SIEM; alternatively we can retain logs in our EU audit store under contract for 12 months.

3) KV cache and prefix caching
- These operate in-memory on the serving layer and are not written to persistent object storage. Eviction happens at session end or according to configured TTL.

4) Options we can include in SOW / MSA
- Contract clause: "no retention of raw prompts/outputs in Hosted unless explicitly enabled in writing"
- Dedicated residency SLA and KMS integration clause
- Audit/export integration to HealthIQ Splunk (secure forwarder / S3 export + signed delivery)

Attachments: I’ve attached our security pack (redacted SOC2 summary, encryption architecture diagram) and a short retention wording template you can drop into the MSA. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleSecurityPack

Let me know if you want a quick 30-minute technical readout for procurement — happy to join.

—
Ben Carter
